description: Recon Village presentations from DEF CON 26 covering reconnaissance, OSINT techniques, and information gathering methodologies for security research and penetration testing.

talks.title: Building Visualisation Platforms for OSINT Data Using OSS
talks.teaser: Workshop on building OSINT visualization platforms using free and open source tools to gain actionable intelligence.
talks.summary:
Reconnaissance and Insights

Reconnaissance is about gathering information, but raw data has little value without actionable insights. Most research focuses on finding data rather than converting it into decisions.

Visualization Approach

The workshop covers gathering, storing, processing, and visualizing OSINT data using free open source solutions. Visualization alone is insufficient; metrics must answer business questions and lead to actionable decisions.

Workflow Steps

Gathering OSINT data, storing it, processing and visualizing, then gaining insights comprise the workshop methodology.

Practical Use Cases

Monitoring SSL/TLS certificates, domains and subdomains in near-real time. Creating dashboards from public datasets like scans.io to understand organizational external posture. Building monitoring and alerting solutions using OSINT data for business decisions.

Deliverables

Participants receive step-by-step Gitbook documentation, custom scripts and tools, scenarios for implementation, and data references.

talks.title: skiptracer   Ghetto OSINT for Broke Hackers
talks.teaser: Low-cost OSINT tool using web scraping to gather PII and passive information on targets without paid services.
talks.summary:
Budget Reconnaissance Challenge

Initial recon vectors typically use paid-for data, APIs like Recon-NG, or transforms like Maltego. These tools require budget many researchers lack.

Skiptracer Solution

Using basic Python web scraping of PII paywall sites enables passive target information gathering on a budget. The tool compiles information from free sources rather than paid databases.

Gathered Information

Modules support queries for phone numbers, emails, screen names, real names, addresses, IPs, hostnames, breach credentials, and more.

Practical Guidance

The demo covers tool usage, problems and pitfalls with scrapers, and how the tool helps expand attack surface knowledge. Relevant target information is collected efficiently without budget constraints.

talks.title: Introducing YOGA Your OSINT Graphical Analyzer
talks.teaser: YOGA tool answers the critical OSINT question 'What do I do now?' when you have one data type and need more.
talks.summary:
Data Pivot Challenge

Reconnaissance and OSINT investigations involve gathering data from numerous sources. The biggest challenge is taking gathered data and transforming it into additional information.

YOGA Tool

Your OSINT Graphical Analyzer (YOGA) addresses the most common data-gathering question: "What do I do now?" when you have email addresses or other data types.

Design Approach

YOGA is designed to help when you have one data type and need to know different actions to get more data. Resources like osintframework.com and similar bookmark collections are overwhelming.

Usage and Extension

The tool helps teams use and extend capabilities in their work. Attendees learn how to apply YOGA in their reconnaissance and investigation processes.

talks.title: Core OSINT Keeping Track of and Reporting All the Things
talks.teaser: Methods for managing massive OSINT investigation data and ensuring comprehensive coverage of all pivot points.
talks.summary:
Investigation Data Overload

OSINT investigations generate massive amounts of data: CSVs, text output, images, URLs. Tracking all this data and ensuring complete pivot point coverage is challenging.

Standard Operating Procedures

Successful investigators maintain SOPs defining their process. They run tools, use sock puppets, scrape websites, and find extensive data requiring organization.

Data Management Challenge

OSINTers, pentesters, defenders, and PIs easily get swamped in data. Keeping investigations on track is critical for comprehensive results.

Management Methods

The presentation examines bad, good, and amazing methods for keeping investigations organized, ensuring no pivot points are missed, and maintaining the ability to report findings effectively.

talks.title: Prebellico 100 Perfect Passive Pre-engagement/Post Compromise
talks.teaser: 100% passive intelligence gathering on internal networks using weak assumptions about target environment.
talks.summary:
Internal Network Intelligence

When attacking modern internal networks, intelligence determines success. Understanding the environment prevents missing targets of opportunity.

Passive Information Gathering

Obtaining stealthy environment information in mature environments is difficult. Even in overt engagements, limited time windows create challenges.

Assumptions

Internal testing often operates on incorrect assumptions about switched networks. These assumptions drive engagement methods but may be wrong.

Prebellico Framework

Prebellico enables pre-engagement and post-compromise intelligence gathering through 100% passive methods using minimal resources. It gathers information about system intent, internal address space, hostnames, egress filtering, TCP trust relationships, and open ports through passive reverse port scanning techniques.

talks.title: Opening Note
talks.teaser: Opening remarks for DEF CON 26 Recon Village.
talks.summary:
### Welcoming the DEF CON 26 Recon Village
At 00:00, Recon Village lead coordinator Sudhanshu Chauhan welcomes attendees to DEF CON 26, reflecting on the community's enthusiastic reception and the growing importance of Open Source Intelligence (OSINT).

### Overview of Village Tracks, Tool Demos, and CTF
At 01:01, Chauhan outlines the weekend's schedule, highlighting expert technical lectures, live open-source tool demonstration stages, and the annual OSINT capture-the-flag (CTF) tournament designed to challenge investigative methodology.

### Empowering Grassroots Tool Development
At 02:00, the speaker emphasizes the village's mission to nurture grassroots open-source tooling. He encourages aspiring researchers to publish and share custom automation scripts, noting that community encouragement and peer feedback are vital for advancing the OSINT ecosystem.

### Setting the Stage for Investigative Keynotes
Concluding at 03:01, Chauhan introduces the track organizers and hands over the stage to commence the village's keynote presentations and collaborative research workshops.

talks.title: Closing Note
talks.teaser: Closing remarks for DEF CON 26 Recon Village.
talks.summary:
### Recon Village Concluding Remarks
At 00:00, organizers upgoingstar and Sudhanshu C deliver the official closing notes for the Recon Village at DEF CON 26. The speakers reflect on the community engagement, technical depth, and collaborative atmosphere across the village over the conference weekend.

### Celebrating Open Source Intelligence and Community Research
At 00:45 and 01:40, the organizers express gratitude to the village speakers, attendees, volunteers, and sponsors. They highlight the diverse array of open-source intelligence (OSINT) and asset discovery techniques showcased, and invite participants to contribute to upcoming village workshops and CTF challenges for DEF CON 27.

talks.title: Winning a SANS 504 CTF without winning a SANS CTF
talks.teaser: Using reconnaissance and social engineering to manipulate security professionals and win CTF challenges.
talks.summary:
Social Engineering Challenge

A SANS instructor challenged to socially engineer CTF answers. Choosing personal challenge, the attacker used reconnaissance and social engineering.

Modern Exploitation

Modern technology designed for connectivity and convenience can be exploited by skilled attackers. Facebook and Google lost significant money to similar techniques.

Reconnaissance and Technology

Good reconnaissance combined with modern technology enables attackers to manipulate even vigilant security professionals. The technique works despite threats from the instructor's ex-Navy Seal background.

Walking Away

Successful exploitation allows winning challenge coins without technically winning the CTF, demonstrating the power of social engineering in security contexts.

talks.title: Targeted User Analytics and Human Honeypots
talks.teaser: Using LinkedIn mining and user analytics to predict who will be targeted and how to defend them.
talks.summary:
Targeting Intelligence

Adversaries knowing who to target, how, and where determines breach success. Most corporations fail to use the largest targeting data collection available on public internet.

LinkedIn Analysis

LinkedIn represents the largest business social networking data available to unauthenticated persons. Advanced techniques mine this data to identify and enrich targets.

Targeted User Analytics

Targeted User Analytics and Human Honeypots research identifies and models targeting methods to tip defense scales in favor of defenders. Data-driven threat models using public internet information match adversary approaches.

Defensive Prediction

Analytics predict who will be targeted and why they're vulnerable. Proactive action defends users and assets before compromise attempts occur.

talks.title: 1983 Im born 2018 Im taking on the bad guys
talks.teaser: Using open source tools and techniques to combat modern slavery, wildlife trafficking, and organized crime.
talks.summary:
Non-Traditional OSINT Application

Not a programmer or hacker in the traditional sense, but using open source tools and methodologies to combat modern slavery, wildlife trafficking, terrorism, and serious organized crime.

Open Source Approach

Combining open source resources addresses bigger problems than typically considered in security. Smallest contributions can have profound impact.

Investigative Methodology

Open source investigations follow persons rather than digital fingerprints. Understanding and putting a face to serious organized crimes requires specific methodologies and tools.

Real-World Examples

Recent open source investigations detail methodologies and tools used. The approach works from London financial district offices against worldwide organized crime.

talks.title: WhiteRabbit Combining Threat Intelligence Public Blockchain
talks.teaser: Machine learning model using Bitcoin transaction data to identify illegal cryptocurrency addresses.
talks.summary:
Cryptocurrency Crime

Bitcoin transactions involving illegal activities can be identified through analysis of transaction patterns and connected addresses.

Machine Learning Approach

A machine learning model merges cyber-related information with BTC transaction data. Both private and public sector security professionals can use it to identify criminal activity or build legal cases for stolen coin recovery.

Dataset Construction

Identifying BTC addresses involved in illegal activity provides starting points. Navigation along the chain reconstructs clusters of connected "dirty" addresses using FIFO rules to label them.

Behavioral Classification

Characteristic behavioral analysis determines malicious features for machine learning classification of new addresses. A three-part framework collects clean/dirty address datasets, tests classification models, and predicts address classification.

talks.title: Hacking the international RFQ Process killthebuzzwords
talks.teaser: Exploiting RFP/RFQ procurement processes to discover confidential organizational information.
talks.summary:
Procurement Vulnerability

Large corporate companies issue RFPs and RFQs for security services, often containing classified information like network diagrams and architectural designs.

Public Exposure

Companies issue public RFQs containing confidential and secret information that would typically require extensive enumeration or network access to discover. Information needed for attacks is publicly available through procurement processes.

Attack Surface

Targeting procurement processes exposes a largely unexplored attack surface. Information gathered from RFQs provides extensive confidential details supporting targeted attacks.

Practical Examples

The presentation demonstrates large international organizations failing at RFP/RFQ processes. Attackers often gain access to extensive organizational information supporting attacks likened to insider knowledge without extensive enumeration.

talks.title: Hackathon Product Showcase
talks.teaser: Showcase of hackathon projects developed during DEF CON 26 Recon Village competition.
talks.summary:
Social Engineering and Human-Oriented Security

This presentation explores social engineering attacks and human vulnerability in security systems. Topics include psychological manipulation, pretexting, credential harvesting, phishing techniques, and how attackers exploit human nature to bypass technical defenses in organizations.

talks.title: Supercharge Your Web Recon With Commonspeak
talks.teaser: Evolutionary wordlist generation tool using Google BigQuery datasets for web application reconnaissance.
talks.summary:
Web Recon Wordlists

Web application penetration testing requires understanding attack surface through large realistic wordlists of directories, files, and domains.

Commonspeak Tool

Commonspeak leverages Google's BigQuery platform to generate evolutionary wordlists reflecting current internet trends. Frequent dataset updates enable current wordlist generation.

Dataset Sources

Queries on BigQuery datasets including HTTPArchive, Stack Overflow, and HackerNews parse URLs to build realistic wordlists of directories, files, parameter names, and subdomains.

Commonspeak 2 Features

Scheduled wordlist creation, comprehensive GitHub queries, permutation engines for subdomain discovery, and asynchronous generation provide enhanced capabilities for modern reconnaissance.

talks.title: I fought the law and law lost   Video
talks.teaser: Analysis of multiple database leaks from Argentine security forces revealing private citizen and law enforcement data.
talks.summary:
Police Database Exposure

Argentina's Federal and Buenos Aires City Police experienced significant database leaks, each becoming national scandals.

Leaked Databases

Police Reports database leaks disclosed private information of criminals, informants, involved officers, and original reporters. Database contained drug trafficking and proxenetism cases.

Intelligence Leaks

Proyecto X intelligence task force database leaked sensitive information. The SNIC (Criminal Information National System) exposed intelligence on criminal gangs under federal investigation.

Personal Information Exposure

Buenos Aires City Police entire database exposure revealed every officer's personal information including religious beliefs, health concerns, STDs, clinical and psychological history, demonstrating serious security failures.

talks.title: Adventures in the dark web of government data
talks.teaser: Mining US federal government databases, especially FCC data, for geolocation and infrastructure discovery.
talks.summary:
Government Data OSINT

The US federal government produces tens of thousands of forms collecting data on oil wells, imported vehicles, cell tower locations, and more. Most data remains locked behind outdated search interfaces or database formats.

Database Coverage

Scrapers and parsers work with hundreds of databases containing OSINT treasures outside Google and LexisNexis indexes. Coaxing OSINT from messy, hard-to-find data requires specialized techniques.

FCC Data Deep Dive

Over 20 million FCC licenses for regulated spectrum transmission leave data residue useful for geolocation of border surveillance infrastructure and McDonald's drive-thru radio frequencies.

Data Combination

Combining transmission protocols with contextual public data enables investigation. Automated Identification System signals on cargo ships joined with shipping records reveal what ships carry.

talks.title: Applied OSINT For Politics Turning Open Data Into News
talks.teaser: Applying OSINT techniques to investigate politicians and public figures, turning data into news stories.
talks.summary:
Political Investigation

Open source intelligence techniques apply to politicians, candidates, and others holding public trust. Combining investigation methods turns data into news stories even when incomplete.

General Principles

The presentation outlines general principles for investigating public figures and taking information to create news coverage.

Case Studies

Selling out before financial crisis through insider stock trades. Family money laundering of campaign contributions. Purchasing homes at steep discounts from campaign donors. Wasteful use of public funds for office decoration. Actual voter fraud by political candidates.

Data-Driven Investigation

These case studies demonstrate combining OSINT techniques effectively to expose wrongdoing and create newsworthy stories about public figure misconduct.

talks.title: KEYNOTE   From Breach to Bust
talks.teaser: Keynote on analyzing breaches and investigation techniques from breach to legal action.
talks.summary:
### Keynote: Tracing Adversaries From Breach to Bust
At 00:00, Andrew Macpherson (Andrew Mohawk) delivers the DEF CON 26 Recon Village Keynote, presenting advanced entity-relationship graph analysis techniques for tracing cybercriminals from initial corporate data breaches to real-world attribution.

### Ingesting and Structuring Compromised Data
At 07:00, Macpherson explores the processing of unstructured breach datasets. Corporate leaks, underground forum dumps, and stolen credential collections contain millions of disparate data points—including email addresses, IP logs, usernames, and cryptocurrency addresses—that must be normalized for automated analysis.

### Visual Layouts and Relational Graph Models
At 14:01, the speaker demonstrates how graph algorithms reveal hidden relational patterns. Rather than analyzing spreadsheets, plotting breach indicators as interconnected nodes and edges allows investigators to identify central communication hubs, shared hosting servers, and common administrative personas.

### Case Studies: Piercing Online Anonymity
At 21:02 and 28:00, Macpherson walks through real-world forensic investigations. By pivoting across WHOIS registration records, forum post timestamps, and leaked database hashes using custom Maltego transforms, he illustrates how subtle operational security (OPSEC) failures unmask pseudonymous threat actors.

### Ethical Governance and Privacy in OSINT Investigations
Concluding at 35:01, Macpherson addresses the ethical and regulatory boundaries of OSINT research. He discusses data protection standards (including GDPR), the risks of aggregating non-consensual personal data, and the professional responsibility investigators carry when managing sensitive intelligence.

talks.title: Bug Bounty Hunting on Steroids
talks.teaser: Automating bug bounty hunting through continuous monitoring and reconnaissance task optimization.
talks.summary:
Bug Bounty Challenges

Bug bounty researchers repeat tedious tasks: monitoring for targets, checking common issues, remembering tool flags. Small improvements accumulate, but a better approach exists.

Automation Machine

A bug hunting machine that is always watching, reacts to new targets, handles repetitive tasks, integrates new tools easily, scales affordably, and improves offensive capacity through battle-tested development technologies.

Approach

Bug Bounty Hunting on Steroids leverages development lessons to improve research automation and productivity. Research shares lessons learned and battle-tested approaches.

Applications

The machine monitors own infrastructure to defend against hackers before they can, saving bug bounty payouts. Frameworks discussed will be open sourced with the presentation.

talks.title: Mapping wifi networks for interesting traffic patterns
talks.teaser: WiFi network mapping tool showing all connected devices and enabling bandwidth monitoring and device detection.
talks.summary:
WiFi Network Discovery

WiFi hacking tools like airmon-ng and kismet have existed for years. Trackerjacker provides new capabilities for viewing networks and connected devices.

Trackerjacker Features

See all networks in an area and all devices connected to each network. Know who's hogging bandwidth (and potentially deauth them). Detect when someone's cell phone is nearby. Monitor if Airbnb host IP cameras upload to cloud.

Radio Space Intelligence

Exploring surprisingly-informative data floating around in radio space reveals network and device information otherwise invisible.

Skill Development

Attendees gain new radio hacking skill points and a new tool for reconnaissance and network analysis.

talks.title: Stalker In A Haystack
talks.teaser: Detecting if you're being monitored via Twitter and identifying who is stalking or monitoring you.
talks.summary:
Stalking Detection

Following targets on Twitter directly arouses suspicion. Stalkers can hide in follower lists without direct follows.

Strawman Technique

Stalkers follow everyone but the target to monitor without detection. Suspicious patterns reveal hidden monitoring.

Monitoring Discovery

Stalker In A Haystack teaches techniques to determine if you are being monitored via Twitter and identify who is doing it.

Defensive OSINT

Understanding how stalkers hide in follower lists enables discovery of those lying in shadows, providing defensive awareness against undetected monitoring.

talks.title: How WHOIS Data Uncovered $32b Connected to  Mormon Church
talks.teaser: WHOIS data analysis uncovering $32 billion in assets connected to the Mormon Church.
talks.summary:
Financial Mystery

The Mormon Church's finances have been mostly opaque despite suspicions of billions in wealth and stock market investments. In May 2018, MormonLeaks released compiled information connecting $32 billion to the Church.

WHOIS Methodology

It all started with WHOIS data analysis and was verified through publicly available open sources.

Investigation Results

The entire story demonstrates how public data and techniques reveal financial information about organizations maintaining opacity. WHOIS data combined with public sources creates comprehensive financial pictures.

Open Source Impact

Public information analysis proves effective at uncovering organizational financial details when compiled and analyzed systematically.

talks.title: Emergent Recon   fresh methodology and tools for hackers in 201
talks.teaser: Modern recon methodology focusing on asset discovery, enumeration, and workflow automation for 2018.
talks.summary:
Recon Evolution

Reconnaissance is both art and science. The landscape for finding attack targets continuously changes. Whether called "Asset Discovery" or something else, it remains core to bounty hunting and red team work.

Methodology Focus

Jason Haddix expands his ever-changing recon methodology, discussing which tools to use and which to avoid.

New Methods and Frameworks

The presentation outlines new methods coined in 2018 plus frameworks automating and documenting workflow. Topics include brand/TLD discovery, host enumeration, application threat modeling, and more.

Workflow Documentation

Automation frameworks enable consistent methodology application and documentation of reconnaissance processes, improving efficiency and repeatability.

talks.title: Mapping Social Media with Facial Recognition
talks.teaser: Social Mapper uses facial recognition to automatically correlate social media profiles across sites at scale.
talks.summary:
Automated Profile Discovery

Manual social media reconnaissance is time-consuming, typically starting with finding online presence across various platforms. Automation on mass scale with hundreds or thousands of targets is possible.

Facial Recognition Integration

Social Mapper uses facial recognition to correlate social media profiles across different sites on large scale. Automated searching of popular social media for targets names and pictures detects and groups individuals' presence.

Output and Applications

Results output to reports for quick operator review. Facial recognition removes false positives, enabling faster review. Use cases include automated gathering of social media profiles for targeted phishing campaigns.

Platform Support

Social Mapper supports LinkedIn, Facebook, Twitter, Google Plus, Instagram, VKontakte, Weibo, and Douban with input from organization names, image folders, or CSV files with names and image URLs.

talks.title: OpenPiMap Hacking the hackers with OSINT Raspberry Pis
talks.teaser: Low-cost Raspberry Pi-based network monitoring using Netflow and OSINT to detect malicious traffic.
talks.summary:
Home Network Defense

OpenPiMap is a network utility detecting, analyzing, and responding to malicious network traffic on small home or office networks. Running on 5v Raspberry Pi costing under $10 provides dynamic interactive threat response.

Detection Approach

Everyday internet-facing systems face thousands of scans and exploit attempts with minimal notification. OpenPiMap detects and responds to botnets, hackers, and script kiddies traditional firewalls ignore.

Technical Stack

The open source Python3, Flask, JavaScript, and SQLite tool combines open source intelligence with networking and intrusion detection. Two-part architecture: Netflow collection and database processing.

Malicious Detection

All traffic is compared to dozens of IP blacklists. Identified suspects are mapped, interrogated via Shodan API for services and ownership, and staged for exploitation if available exploits exist.
